newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO BECOMES 'FREE AGENT' AFTER $27.5M PAYMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO BECOMES 'FREE AGENT' AFTER $27.5M PAYMENT.

text.p: Ronaldo's lawyer said on Friday he had paid the four billion pesetas ($27.5 million) necessary to release the Brazilian striker Ronaldo from his contract with Barcelona.
Although the payment technically makes Ronaldo a free agent, a UEFA circular has decreed that only Spanish clubs are allowed to sign him without negotiating with Barcelona.
Italian club Inter Milan are hoping to buy Ronaldo, who is currently in Bolivia with the Brazilian national side.
"From today the player no longer belongs to Barcelona," said Fernando Rey, the Brazilian's lawyer.
Negotiations to keep Ronaldo at Barcelona broke down at the end of last month.
The International Association of Players' Agents (IAFA), meanwhile, has urged the European Commission to judge on a FIFA ruling which is preventing Ronaldo from joining Inter Milan.
A Commission spokesman on Friday confirmed that the Commission had received the letter but declined to comment further.
Barcelona have invoked the FIFA ruling as a last-ditch effort to stop Ronaldo from moving to Internazionale.
IAFA claims that FIFA ruling 616, issued early in June, reintroduced the system, until 1999, of payments of a transfer fee for non-EU players who were at the end of their contracts.
The transfer fee system was abolished only last March.
The ruling also stated that, regarding international transfers, a federation could refuse to provide a transfer certificate if a player had ended a contract unilaterally.
